answer.rationale: Outside servicing personnel must mutually inform the on-site and outside employers of their respective lockout/tagout procedures only when they will perform activities covered by the scope and application of the lockout/tagout standard. Covered servicing or maintenance exists where unexpected energization, startup, or release of stored energy could occur and cause injury. The scenario confirms outside-vendor routine maintenance but does not establish that hazard predicate.
answer.missing_information_or_escalation_reason: Determine whether the maintenance exposes employees to a potential unexpected energization, startup, or release of stored/residual energy that could cause injury. If yes, the work is covered and the on-site and outside employers must inform each other of their respective lockout/tagout procedures.
